target: hypertools/io/save.py (hyp.save / hyp.io.save) -- pickle-based object serialization and its round-trip through hyp.load. Enumerated surface: save(obj, fname, **kwargs); function docstring is a single line ('Pickle `obj` to `fname`.'); module docstring documents the pickle trust model, states figure/animation export is NOT handled here ('lands in Plan 6 (plot)'; 'A figure passed here is pickled like any other object; the format-aware exporter comes later'), and that there is no geo special-casing. findings.title: A failed save destroys the pre-existing file at the target path (truncate-before-pickle, non-atomic write)
findings.description: save() opens fname with mode 'wb' (truncating any existing file to 0 bytes) BEFORE pickle.dump runs. If pickling then fails -- e.g. the object contains a lambda, generator, open file handle, thread lock, a HyperAnimation (F20-save-004), or a fitted Pipeline (F20-save-011) -- the user's previously saved good data at that path is irreversibly destroyed and a 0-byte corrupt stub is left behind. Verified in both passes: an 8152-byte good pickle went to 0 bytes (lambda payload), and a 246-byte good pickle went to 0 bytes (generator payload); reload then raises a bare 'EOFError: Ran out of input'. Realistic trigger: a scientist re-saves an updated results dict that accidentally acquired an unpicklable member. Standard fix is an atomic write (dump to a temp file in the same directory, then os.replace), which also removes the corrupt-stub-on-new-path behavior.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
p = '/tmp/precious.pkl'
hyp.save(np.arange(1000.0), p)          # good file on disk
try:
    hyp.save(lambda x: x, p)            # fails mid-save
except Exception as e:
    print('save failed:', e)
import os; print('bytes left:', os.path.getsize(p))  # 0
hyp.load(p)                              # EOFError -- original data gone
findings.expected: A failed save leaves the previous file contents untouched (atomic write), or at minimum documents that the target is truncated before serialization.
findings.actual: pass 2: saving generator raised: TypeError: cannot pickle 'generator' object | pre-existing good file: 246B before failed save, 0B after (DESTROYED: True) | reloading the file after failed save: EOFError: Ran out of input || pass 1: file size 8152 -> 0 bytes; file NO LONGER LOADS: EOFError: Ran out of input

findings.title: save() silently ignores the file extension: data.csv/.npy/.mat/.xlsx/fig.png are all pickles, invalid in their nominal formats
findings.description: save() always writes a pickle regardless of extension, with no warning. hyp.load round-trips every such file EXACTLY (its b'\x80' byte-sniff rescues them), but the files are lies to every other tool: data.npy fails np.load ('ValueError: This file contains pickled (object) data'), data.csv fails pd.read_csv and data.json fails json.load ('UnicodeDecodeError: ... byte 0x80 in position 0'), data.mat fails scipy.io.loadmat ('ValueError: Unknown mat file type, version 95, 117'), data.xlsx fails pd.read_excel, and hyp.save(fig, 'figure.png') produces a 'PNG' that plt.imread rejects ('SyntaxError: not a PNG file') -- even though the real figure exporter hyp.plot(..., save_path='fig.png') exists. This is asymmetric with hyp.load, which genuinely parses .npy/.npz/.csv/.tsv/.txt/.json/.parquet/.mat/.xlsx/.xls. A warning (or format dispatch, see F20-save-009) on recognized non-pickle extensions would prevent silently misleading files that scientists then hand to collaborators, Excel, or MATLAB. Unpickling such a mislabeled file also requires pickle's arbitrary-code-execution trust model.
findings.repro:
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
df = pd.DataFrame({'a': [1.0, 2.0], 'b': [3.0, 4.0]})
hyp.save(df, '/tmp/data.csv')      # no warning
pd.read_csv('/tmp/data.csv')       # UnicodeDecodeError
hyp.save(df, '/tmp/data.npy')
np.load('/tmp/data.npy', allow_pickle=False)  # ValueError
findings.expected: Either format-aware writing keyed on extension (mirroring load), or a UserWarning that a pickle is being written under a non-pickle extension.
findings.actual: data.npy magic=b'\x80\x04\x95e' ... INVALID as .npy: ValueError: This file contains pickled (object) data. | data.csv ... UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 0 | data.mat ... ValueError: Unknown mat file type, version 95, 117 | figure.png: real PNG=False; plt.imread fails: SyntaxError: not a PNG file. All 17 files written as pickle bytes: True (pass 2: all 15 re-tested extensions begin b'\x80\x04')

findings.title: Round-trip silently returns the WRONG dataset when the saved filename collides with a dataset name (save(x,'iris') -> load('iris') = sklearn iris)
findings.description: save() writes to any bare filename, but load()'s resolution chain checks built-in example names and sklearn/seaborn dataset names BEFORE local files. Verified across both passes with three resolver families: after hyp.save(arr, 'iris'), hyp.load('iris') silently returns scikit-learn's iris DataFrame; after hyp.save(arr, 'penguins'), hyp.load('penguins') returns seaborn's penguins (344, 7); after hyp.save(arr, 'weights'), hyp.load('weights') returns the hosted 36-subject fMRI dataset -- never the user's saved data. No error, no warning: silently wrong data. The shadowing is documented in load()'s docstring (and load('./name') recovers the file, verified), but save()'s one-line docstring gives no hint, and save() could easily warn when fname (no path separator, no extension) matches a shadowing dataset name.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, os, tempfile, hypertools as hyp
os.chdir(tempfile.mkdtemp())
arr = np.arange(12.0).reshape(4, 3)
hyp.save(arr, 'penguins')
out = hyp.load('penguins')
print(type(out), getattr(out, 'shape', None))  # DataFrame (344, 7) -- not arr
print(np.array_equal(hyp.load('./penguins'), arr))  # True -- workaround
findings.expected: Round-tripping a file you just saved returns your data, or save()/load() warns about the name collision.
findings.actual: hyp.load('penguins') -> DataFrame shape=(344, 7); got my file back: False | SHADOWED: load('iris') returned DataFrame (cols ['sepal length (cm)', ...]) instead of the saved array | SHADOWED: load('weights') returned the hosted dataset (list of 36 arrays) | load('./penguins') -> ndarray; got my file back: True

findings.title: hyp.save crashes on the return of hyp.plot(animate=True) (HyperAnimation) with a cryptic internals-leaking error
findings.description: hyp.plot(..., animate=True) returns a HyperAnimation, and the io/save.py module docstring says a figure passed to save 'is pickled like any other object' -- but a HyperAnimation is not picklable: hyp.save(anim, 'anim.pkl') raises AttributeError naming the internal local function '_draw.<locals>.update_lines_parallel', with no hint that the supported export path is HyperAnimation.save('anim.gif') (hypertools/plot/hyper_animation.py:59) or hyp.plot(..., save_path=...). findings.title: save() accepts **kwargs but silently ignores all of them (protocol=, compression=, typos)
findings.description: save(obj, fname, **kwargs) swallows every keyword argument without effect or warning. Verified: hyp.save(arr, f, protocol=0) still writes a protocol-4 pickle (file byte-identical to the default; a protocol-0 pickle would be ASCII); compression='gzip' writes an uncompressed pickle (magic b'\x80\x04', not gzip's b'\x1f\x8b'); format='csv', fmt='npy', and typo kwargs (fnme='oops.pkl', overwrite=False) are accepted silently. A user who explicitly requests protocol=2 for compatibility with an older Python silently gets protocol-4/5 files that their target environment may not read. Either forward kwargs to pickle.dump (protocol/fix_imports/buffer_callback are the natural ones) or drop **kwargs so typos raise TypeError.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.save(np.arange(5), '/tmp/p0.pkl', protocol=0)
print(open('/tmp/p0.pkl', 'rb').read(2))  # b'\x80\x04' -- protocol arg ignored
hyp.save(np.arange(5), '/tmp/gz.pkl', compression='gzip', fnme='typo')  # no error
findings.expected: protocol= forwarded to pickle.dump (file starts with protocol-0 ASCII opcodes); unknown kwargs raise TypeError.
findings.actual: kwargs ignored: default=b'\x80\x04' protocol=0->b'\x80\x04' (same bytes: True); compression/format/fmt accepted silently: b'\x80\x04' | pass 1: typo kwargs fnme= and overwrite=False accepted silently, no error

findings.title: save() does not expand '~' or environment variables although load() does (asymmetric path handling)
findings.description: load() applies expanduser(expandvars(...)) to paths (load.py:292), but save() passes fname straight to open(). Verified in both passes: hyp.save(arr, '~/f.pkl') raises FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '~/...' and hyp.save(arr, '$TMPDIR/f20save_env.pkl') likewise -- while hyp.load resolves both forms. So the natural pair save(x, '~/data.pkl') / load('~/data.pkl') fails on the save half. (If a literal '~' directory existed in cwd, the file would even be written there, diverging from where load looks.) One-line fix: open(os.path.expanduser(os.path.expandvars(fname)), 'wb') for str/bytes fnames.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.save(np.arange(3), '~/f20_tilde.pkl')  # FileNotFoundError; hyp.load('~/f20_tilde.pkl') would have expanded
findings.expected: save() resolves '~' and '$VARS' exactly like load() so save/load pairs are symmetric.
findings.actual: tilde path save: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '~/f20save_tilde_test.pkl' | envvar path save: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '$TMPDIR/f20save_env.pkl'

findings.title: Stale module-docstring NOTE: says the format-aware figure exporter 'comes later' / 'lands in Plan 6', but it has already landed
findings.description: hypertools/io/save.py's module docstring states: 'NOTE: figure/animation export (png/pdf/svg/html/gif/mp4) is NOT handled here -- it depends on the plot backends and lands in Plan 6 (plot). A figure passed here is pickled like any other object; the format-aware exporter comes later.' The exporter now exists: hyp.plot has save_path= in its signature (plot.py:173), and HyperAnimation.save (hyper_animation.py:59) chooses a writer by file extension. The forward-looking planning language ('Plan 6', 'comes later') is stale for a 1.0 release and should instead point users at the existing export paths. Also 'pickled like any other object' is false for animations (F20-save-004).
findings.expected: Module note reads e.g.: 'figure/animation export is handled by hyp.plot(..., save_path=...) and HyperAnimation.save(); a figure passed here is pickled instead.'
findings.actual: save.py lines 7-9: 'it depends on the plot backends and lands in Plan 6 (plot). A figure passed here is pickled like any other object; the format-aware exporter comes later.' -- while plot.py line 173 already has 'save_path=None' and hyper_animation.py:59 implements extension-driven save().

findings.title: No format-aware saving despite format-rich load: save cannot write CSV/npy/parquet/etc., and does not create missing parent directories
findings.description: hyp.load parses .npy/.npz/.csv/.tsv/.txt/.json/.parquet/.mat/.xlsx/.xls plus pickles, but hyp.save can only pickle -- there is no extension dispatch, so users must fall back to pandas/numpy for interoperable outputs, and any extension they pass is misleading (F20-save-002). Additionally, saving into a nonexistent nested directory raises a bare FileNotFoundError ('[Errno 2] No such file or directory: .../a/b/c/out.pkl') rather than creating parents; other misuse errors are bare builtins too, most cryptically int fname -> 'OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor' (open() treats ints as OS file descriptors). Suggested 1.x enhancement: extension-driven writers mirroring load's readers, parent-directory creation (or an opt-in mkdir=True) or a HypertoolsIOError naming the missing directory, a TypeError for int fname, and atomic writes (F20-save-001).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.save(np.arange(3), '/tmp/f20_new_dir/a/b/x.pkl')  # FileNotFoundError, no mkdir
hyp.save(np.arange(3), 987)  # OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor
# and no way to produce a real CSV: hyp.save(df, 'x.csv') pickles (see F20-save-002)
findings.expected: save(df, 'x.csv') writes real CSV (etc., mirroring load); parent directories created or clearly diagnosed; non-path fname types rejected with TypeError.
findings.actual: nested nonexistent dirs: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../a/b/c/out.pkl' | int fname (fd semantics!): OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor | all extensions produce pickle bytes (magic b'\x80\x04')

findings.title: Shipped test suite never round-trips hyp.save through hyp.load
findings.description: tests/io/test_save.py contains only two tests: one saves an array and reloads it with raw pickle.load (not hyp.load), the other only checks hyp.save is callable and the file exists (re-run in pass 2: '2 passed in 1.97s'). No shipped test covers the save->hyp.load round-trip, DataFrame/index/dtype fidelity, list-of-arrays, fitted-model persistence, or any failure path -- the pairing where the shadowing (F20-save-003), data-loss (F20-save-001), and Pipeline (F20-save-011) behaviors live is untested. Not a runtime defect; filed for release-hardening visibility.
findings.expected: At least one test asserting hyp.load(hyp.save(...)) returns the exact object (values, dtype, index/columns), plus a fitted-model round-trip test.
findings.actual: test_save_roundtrips_array uses 'with open(fname, "rb") as f: loaded = pickle.load(f)' and 'np.allclose' only; test_hyp_save_and_io_exposed only asserts os.path.exists(fname).

findings.title: hyp.save cannot save a fitted hypertools.Pipeline (or any plot/analyze return_model result containing one) -- lambdas in _make_stage_step make every Pipeline unpicklable
findings.description: save.py's module docstring says save() 'pickles a hypertools result (array / DataFrame / list / fitted model)', and hyp.plot's docstring advertises the return_model=True dict's 'pipeline' as 'reusable via hyp.plot(new_data, pipeline=...)'. But hypertools.core.pipeline._make_stage_step (pipeline.py:420-448) builds every stage step as a _DispatchStep wrapping a module-local lambda (e.g. `lambda data, m: _reduce(data, reduce=m, ndims=ndims, ...)`), so pickling ANY Pipeline -- and therefore the entire return_model dict -- raises `AttributeError: Can't get local object '_make_stage_step.<locals>.<lambda>'`. A scientist who fits a pipeline on session-1 data cannot persist it for session 2; the cross-session reuse story breaks exactly at the save step, with a cryptic internals-leaking error (and, per F20-save-001, destruction of any existing file at the target path). Per-key isolation proved every other return_model component pickles fine (fig: Figure OK, models: dict OK, xform_data: list OK, animation/predict: None OK); only 'pipeline' fails. The standalone fitted Reducer DOES pickle and reproduces transforms on new data exactly (verified), so this is specific to the Pipeline stage wrappers. Fix: replace the lambdas with module-level functions or functools.partial over module-level callables (or implement __reduce__ on _DispatchStep).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
w = hyp.load('weights_sample')
out = hyp.plot(w, reduce='PCA', ndims=3, return_model=True)
hyp.save(out['pipeline'], '/tmp/pipe.pkl')  # AttributeError
# hyp.save(out, '/tmp/model.pkl')  # same failure via the dict
findings.expected: Pipeline (and the whole return_model dict) saves and reloads, so `hyp.plot(new_data, pipeline=hyp.load('/tmp/pipe.pkl'))` works across sessions, matching the 'fitted model' claim in save.py's docstring.
findings.actual: return_model dict save FAILED: AttributeError: Can't get local object '_make_stage_step.<locals>.<lambda>' | isolation: save(out['pipeline']) type=Pipeline: AttributeError: Can't get local object '_make_stage_step.<locals>.<lambda>'; all five other keys saved OK

findings.title: Cross-unit (load) doc inaccuracies hit during save round-trips: 'spiral' is a list of two arrays (docstring says 'numpy array'); legacy=True on a 1.0-saved pickle misdiagnoses it as 'deepdish/HDF5-format'
findings.description: (1) load()'s docstring: '`spiral` is numpy array containing data for a 3D spiral' -- actually hyp.load('spiral') returns a list of 2 arrays, each (1000, 3); np.asarray on it is 3-D and crashes downstream reducers ('ValueError: Found array with dim 3, while dim <= 2 is required by PCA'). (2) hyp.load(path, legacy=True) on a pickle that hyp.save just wrote raises HypertoolsIOError asserting 'This looks like a legacy (<1.0) deepdish/HDF5-format dataset' without any content check -- a misleading diagnosis for a modern pickle (the flag forces the legacy path unconditionally). Both verified by real runs during this audit; primary ownership belongs to the F-load unit but recorded here since they surfaced in save round-trip flows.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
s = hyp.load('spiral'); print(type(s), [np.asarray(x).shape for x in s])
hyp.save(np.eye(3), '/tmp/modern.pkl')
hyp.load('/tmp/modern.pkl', legacy=True)  # HypertoolsIOError about deepdish/HDF5
findings.expected: (1) docstring: 'a list of two (1000, 3) arrays'; (2) legacy loader sniffs for an actual HDF5/deepdish payload (or the message hedges) before asserting the file's format.
findings.actual: <class 'list'> 2 / [(1000, 3), (1000, 3)] | legacy=True on 1.0 pickle: HypertoolsIOError: This looks like a legacy (<1.0) deepdish/HDF5-format dataset. Reading it needs the `deepdish` package...
